newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil seen $0.50-$1 down, Brent 10 cents down.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil seen $0.50-$1 down, Brent 10 cents down.

text.p: IPE Brent and gas oil futures were expected to open weaker on Thursday, reflecting softer sentiment in New York markets overnight, brokers said.
May gas oil, which settled $3 up at $171.75 a tonne on Wednesday, should open between 50 cents and $1 lower.
"Some people are going for $1 but we finished steady yesterday so I don't think it'll come off that far at the open," said a broker, plumping for a call of 50 cents down.
June Brent, which closed at $18.52 a barrel, talked about 10 cents weaker in Singapore, tracking losses in NYMEX ACCESS trade where the prompt crude contract shed 11 cents overnight.
"Brent's also under pressure from the cash market where there were a trades at lower levels last night," said a broker.

June Brent traded as low as $18.39 a barrel for 100 lots in late U.S. dealing after fetching $18.60 in London on Wednesday, traders said. A European major oil company was also active selling July Brent partials on the cash market.
Traders said a narrowing transatlantic arbitrage and firmer physical prices in Europe reduced options for sellers looking to move North Sea barrels out of the region.
Weak U.S. gasoline prices added to the soft tone, brokers said.
IPE Brent also faced an uphill task technically after just failing to fill a chart gap up to $18.77 a barrel. The contract fell two cents short of its target on Wednesday.
Gas oil could lose some momentum after the expiry of the NYMEX May heating oil contract on Wednesday.
"That could potentially remove some support from the front end of the market but the backwardation (in London) would suggest there may be some more fun and games to be seen," said a broker.
European holidays were expected to keep volumes thin.
